title: Disable inactive users
product: Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory
use_case: On a schedule, disable users with no successful sign-in for 30 days, or the days you set, without Sophos ITDR: in on-premises Active Directory for synced users, and in Entra ID for cloud-only users.
trigger: Generic Trigger, Playbook Usage Playbook Schedule. Then add a schedule with More Actions > Schedule Executions, such as daily with the cron expression 0 2 * * *
connections: Taegis.MicrosoftGraphAPI 2.12.2, the Microsoft Graph API connector Sophos manages, to find inactive users, read their directory roles and disable cloud-only accounts
Taegis.LDAP 1.0.13, the Microsoft Active Directory/LDAP connector Sophos manages, through the On-Premise Automation Connector on a data collector, to check and disable synced accounts
requires: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, a Microsoft Graph app with User.Read.All, AuditLog.Read.All, Directory.Read.All and User.EnableDisableAccount.All, Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations, and for synced accounts a Sophos data collector that reaches a domain controller over LDAPS
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook, and it doesn't change what Sophos MDR does.
rollback: Enable User: enable the account again in Active Directory, or in Entra ID for a cloud-only user, and add it to Excluded users so a later run doesn't disable it again.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook disables users with no successful sign-in for the days you set, 30 by default, without Sophos ITDR: in on-premises Active Directory for synced users, and in Entra ID for cloud-only users. A schedule starts it, and it calls the Microsoft Graph API and LDAP connectors Sophos manages, with dry run on, only the domains you list in scope and at most 10 users a run. It needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 and, for synced users, a Sophos data collector that reaches a domain controller.
notes:
Setup:
- It doesn't need Sophos ITDR. Sign-in activity needs Entra ID P1 or P2 and AuditLog.Read.All.
- Set Look-back days to at least the days between runs. Each run then sees only users who became inactive lately, so disabled accounts drop out.
- Graph returns one page per search, 100 users by default. For accounts already inactive when you start, set Look-back days to 0 for a few runs.
- Active Directory accounts that aren't synced to Entra ID aren't found. The LDAP connector looks up one user at a time.
- There's no approval step. Dry run, Domains, Excluded users and Max users per run are the controls.

How it works:
- It searches Microsoft Graph for users whose last successful sign-in, interactive or not, is before midnight UTC Days without a sign-in ago. Graph allows no other filter with sign-in activity, so the playbook drops disabled users, guests and other domains.
- Include users with no sign-in on record adds users with none since December 2023, or ever, created before the cut-off.
- Synced users are disabled in Active Directory only, because Entra Connect Sync would undo a disable in Entra ID. The playbook skips one whose lastLogonTimestamp is newer than the days you set plus 14, because Active Directory updates it only every 9 to 14 days.
- An Active Directory account counts as a match only when its user principal name, sAMAccountName or mail is exactly the user's on-premises name.
- It never disables a user with an Entra ID directory role or in a role-assignable group, or an account with adminCount set. An eligible PIM role that isn't active doesn't count.
- The result is the execution's outcome under Playbooks > Executions.

Testing:
- Not run in a tenant yet.
- On 2026-11-02 the dsl passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings in a Sophos Fusion test tenant, and a renamed copy imported, exported again unchanged apart from the tenant's own fields, and was deleted. It had no identity provider connected.
- Every expression ran in Sophos Fusion's CEL engine, through its evaluateExpr API, in 15 made-up runs: cloud-only, synced, active on-premises, adminCount, already disabled, not found, role holders, excluded, guests, other domains, no sign-in on record, refused disables and a failed search.

Known gaps:
- A real Graph search is untested: whether Graph takes the sign-in activity filter with the $count=true and ConsistencyLevel eventual searchUser always sends, the Look-back days date range, and eq null. A refusal ends the run in FAIL with Graph's message.
- Whether a schedule passes the playbook's settings is untested. Check them in the schedule's Playbook Inputs.
- How the engine runs the per-user loop is untested. It follows the Sophos-managed templates.
- Whether the LDAP connector returns lastLogonTimestamp, userAccountControl and adminCount is untested. Without lastLogonTimestamp, synced users are skipped and the outcome says why.
- Saving the playbook without a connection for a directory you don't have is untested.
